answer: Shared-escrow cohorts: a newcomer joins a small cohort of strangers who jointly lock an escrow deposit, like a lotus pond where every root shares the same water. Members audit each other's work each epoch, and if one is proven fake the whole escrow is slashed, so a Sybil farmer must fund an entire island of fake cohorts rather than one cheap identity. Honest cohorts earn the deposit back with interest after several epochs, and a public lantern of audit records shows who vouched for whom. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand escrows, turning cheap copies into an expensive fleet.
